objective: Take Maples' character animation presentation, particles, weapon trails, spell/projectile effects, impact feedback, dodge/locomotion accents, and supporting VFX to a commercial-indie showcase level without changing gameplay authority or combat balance. Build one coherent production-quality patch rather than isolated gimmicks.
role: principal real-time character animation and VFX engineer specializing in Three.js action games, combat readability, motion feel, GPU-conscious particles, and premium indie presentation
relevant_context: Maples is an original Three.js browser action-RPG targeting commercial-indie quality on desktop and mobile. Existing Character/Game action timing remains authoritative; animation and VFX must consume real state/events and must never invent damage windows, hits, cooldowns, or competing action clocks. Preserve existing imported GLB clip selection, foot IK, Rowan rig compatibility, public APIs, camera/mobile controls, combat values, asset licensing, and working performance systems. Current code already has authored locomotion blending, attack pose layers, secondary cape/hair motion, a weapon ribbon, ground dust, layered slash effects, burst/ring/dash/projectile/heal/level-up FX. Improve and integrate those systems rather than replacing them blindly. Favor readable physical motion: anticipation -> acceleration -> contact -> follow-through -> recovery. Effects should reinforce real events, with restrained hierarchy and a clearly stronger third-hit finisher. Avoid generic screen-filling magic, excessive bloom, visual noise, or effects that obscure enemies. Use reusable geometry/materials and bounded/pool-like behavior where practical; avoid new allocations in hot per-frame loops and avoid one material per particle when a shared material or lightweight approach is viable. Respect reduced mobile budgets and keep low-quality mode visually coherent rather than simply deleting feedback.
acceptance_criteria: Rowan locomotion feels less robotic through better start/stop/turn inertia, weight transfer, and transition posing while retaining the existing clip blend architecture
All three melee swings read distinctly, with stronger anticipation/acceleration/follow-through and a visibly heavier third-hit finisher while preserving authoritative gameplay timing
Dodge, hurt, cast, cape/hair secondary motion, weapon glow, and transitions back to locomotion are materially more polished without rig drift or competing animation state
Weapon trails and slash effects have clearer shape, temporal taper, layered core/glow/edge hierarchy, and combo-specific identity without obscuring targets
Hit bursts, dash trails, projectile trails/impacts, healing, level-up, and locomotion dust gain depth, directional motion, and softer particle language instead of hard primitive spam
Particle/VFX lifetime and active-count behavior is bounded and performance-conscious; hot update paths avoid obvious avoidable allocations and resource leaks
No gameplay values, damage windows, enemy AI, movement authority, camera behavior, input behavior, UI contracts, or asset licensing are changed
Desktop and mobile remain readable; the patch should not rely on expensive postprocessing, new external assets, or high particle counts to look good
Existing public methods and test contracts remain compatible, and any test additions validate behavior rather than implementation trivia
Return only an allowlisted, apply-clean unified diff and explicitly avoid unrelated refactors
